question: Why do important minerals like iron and calcium need active transport to cross the placenta?

options.A: They can only travel when the mother's heart rate is very high
options.B: They are too large to pass through any membrane without being broken down
options.C: They dissolve directly into the amniotic fluid instead of fetal blood
options.D: They are moved against a concentration gradient to ensure the fetus gets enough

explanation: Active transport means the placenta uses energy to pump these minerals in—even if the baby already has more of them than the mother does! Nature makes sure the baby gets what it needs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h5)

question: How do patriarchal community structures contribute to forced marriage?

options.A: By legally requiring women to register businesses in their husband's name
options.B: By forcing young men to marry older women for inheritance
options.C: By banning all forms of traditional marriage ceremonies entirely
options.D: By giving male family members total control over female relatives' lives

explanation: Patriarchal norms concentrate decision-making power in the hands of men, making it easier to override a woman's personal choice. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why is teaching patients how to use home blood pressure monitors such an important nursing duty?

options.A: Patients need to know how to solder broken circuit boards at home
options.B: Good technique prevents false readings that could lead to wrong medication changes
options.C: It stops patients from ever coming back to the hospital clinic
options.D: Home machines are so complicated that only rocket scientists can run them

explanation: If a patient uses poor posture or a bad cuff size at home, their doctor might see bad data and change their prescriptions incorrectly. Your teaching makes a real difference!

question: Why is the membrane inside the lungs where gas exchange happens so incredibly thin?

options.A: To allow the lungs to stretch easily during inhalation
options.B: To reduce the overall weight of the thoracic organs
options.C: To prevent white blood cells from entering the alveoli
options.D: To allow fast and efficient diffusion of gases

explanation: Spot on! A super thin wall means oxygen and carbon dioxide can zip back and forth between your lungs and blood instantly.

question: A patient has severe burns on 40% of their body. Which skin job will be seriously affected?

options.A: Filtering blood plasma
options.B: Digesting dietary fats
options.C: Producing red blood cells
options.D: Making vitamin D

explanation: You got it! Since healthy skin is needed to make vitamin D from sunlight, extensive burns make this process very difficult. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h6)

question: A patient forgets to take their blood pressure meds and misses paying their utility bills. Which daily skill area is struggling?

options.A: Involuntary body reflexes
options.B: Gross motor developmental milestones
options.C: Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs)
options.D: Basic self-care ADLs

explanation: Well done! Managing medications and paying bills require a bit more brainpower and planning, which puts them right into the IADL category.

question: When using a bulb syringe to clear a newborn's airway, which part should you suction first?

options.A: Mouth
options.B: Pharynx
options.C: Trachea
options.D: Nose

explanation: Always suction the mouth before the nose! If you do the nose first, the baby might gasp and accidentally inhale any fluid sitting in their mouth.

question: Why is checking the bladder so important in the first few hours after childbirth?

options.A: Urinary retention always leads to permanent kidney failure
options.B: A full bladder pushes the uterus out of place and causes heavy bleeding
options.C: Bladder fullness is the primary sign of postpartum preeclampsia
options.D: It prevents the lochia from changing from red to white

explanation: Think of it this way: a full bladder takes up space and pushes against the uterus, stopping it from contracting properly. Keeping the bladder empty keeps mom safe from extra bleeding!

question: Which hormone does the outer cell layer (trophoblast) release to keep the corpus luteum going in early pregnancy?

options.A: Luteinizing hormone
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Spot on! That's hCG—the exact hormone pregnancy test strips look for to confirm wonderful news!

question: Why should you keep a client's neck straight and in a neutral position when managing high ICP?

options.A: Straight necks make it easier for the client to chew their meals
options.B: It keeps the breathing tube securely taped to the side of the mouth
options.C: It prevents the client from accidentally pulling out their intravenous lines
options.D: Bending the neck can kink jugular veins and trap blood in the head

explanation: Great to know for clinicals! Twisting or bending the neck blocks blood from draining out of the brain, causing it to back up and shoot up the intracranial pressure.

question: You finish assessing a client in a leg cast and find their toes are cold, pale, and pulseless. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Encourage the patient to walk more to stimulate blood flow
options.B: Wait two hours to see if the circulation returns on its own
options.C: Notify the provider immediately and document the findings
options.D: Remove the cast using hospital scissors immediately

explanation: Cold, pale, pulseless toes indicate severe neurovascular compromise requiring urgent medical evaluation and intervention. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h9)

question: What is the primary fluid collected during a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Synovial joint fluid
options.B: Peritoneal lavage fluid
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: Pleural cavity fluid

explanation: A lumbar puncture specifically targets the subarachnoid space to draw cerebrospinal fluid for laboratory analysis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h1)

question: What mental health challenge do rehabilitation psychologists most commonly help patients work through?

options.A: Physical balance and dizziness
options.B: Nutritional deficits and tube-feeding routines
options.C: Managing acute surgical site pain
options.D: Coping with a sudden disability and grief

explanation: A life-altering illness or injury brings deep emotional pain. Rehab psychologists help patients process these feelings and adapt to their new reality.

question: What type of bowel prep is usually given right before a proctoscopy?

options.A: A 4-liter gallon prep
options.B: Total fasting for 48 hours
options.C: A cleansing enema
options.D: Oral magnesium citrate

explanation: Spot on! Because a proctoscopy only looks at the very end of the bowel, a quick cleansing enema just before the test is usually all it takes to clear the area.

question: A mother just gave birth six hours ago in the maternity ward. Which immediate postpartum emergency should you watch out for most closely?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Chronic pelvic pain

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage (heavy bleeding) is a major postpartum risk, especially in the first few hours after delivery. Always keep a close eye on your patient's lochia and vitals!

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to reduce waste in a hospital store?

options.A: Checking inventory expiration dates every month
options.B: Keeping storage rooms dry, clean, and out of direct sunlight
options.C: Rotating stock properly using FEFO
options.D: Ordering huge quantities far beyond what past data suggests

explanation: You got it! Over-ordering leads straight to expired stock and wasted money—definitely a practice to avoid!

question: A bedridden patient has severely matted hair after weeks of illness. What should you do first?

options.A: Ignore the matting until the patient is fully discharged from the hospital
options.B: Wash the hair with a harsh clarifying shampoo to break apart the tangles
options.C: Cut the matted sections off immediately to save time during the bed bath
options.D: Apply a conditioner or detangling spray and work through small sections with a wide-toothed comb

explanation: Always respect your patient's dignity. Working gently with a lubricant and a wide-toothed comb avoids painful pulling and protects their personal autonomy. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of immediate first aid for a suspected fracture?

options.A: Push any protruding bone ends back inside the skin
options.B: Apply hot packs to the injury site to reduce swelling
options.C: Straighten the deformed limb immediately by pulling hard
options.D: Immobilize the bone to prevent further tissue damage

explanation: Keeping the broken bone still stops sharp edges from tearing nearby blood vessels, nerves, and muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h4)

question: Which of the following is considered a microvascular complication of chronic diabetes?

options.A: Peripheral vascular claudication pain
options.B: Severe hypertension from aortic stenosis
options.C: Coronary artery disease and stroke
options.D: Diabetic retinopathy and nephropathy

explanation: Microvascular complications involve damage to small blood vessels, specifically harming the eyes (retinopathy) and the kidneys (nephropathy). [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why must the healthcare team pause and provide manual ventilation between failed intubation attempts?

options.A: To allow the local anesthetic time to numb the vocal cords fully
options.B: To let the mechanical ventilator automatically calibrate itself
options.C: To cool down the laryngoscope light bulb so it does not burn tissue
options.D: To restore the patient's blood oxygen levels before trying again

explanation: Stopping to ventilate the patient prevents dangerous drops in oxygen saturation while the team regroups. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why is talking about birth control early in post-abortion care so crucial?

options.A: Birth control pills must be taken to prevent future ectopic pregnancies
options.B: Ovulation can return as early as two weeks after the procedure
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives are required to stop ongoing uterine bleeding
options.D: Patients lose natural fertility permanently after a medication abortion

explanation: A patient can actually get pregnant again before their next normal period even arrives, so early counseling is a lifesaver.

question: What triggers a homeostatic imbalance in the human body?

options.A: When a person sleeps for more than eight hours
options.B: When disease or trauma overwhelms normal control systems
options.C: When vital signs stay completely stable for a long time
options.D: When the body eats a balanced diet with fresh fruits

explanation: Well done! When illness or injury hits hard, it can strain or break the natural feedback loops that keep the body balanced.

question: After pricking a finger for blood sugar, why should you wipe away the very first drop?

options.A: It contains tissue fluid that can dilute the sample
options.B: The glucometer machine will reject the first drop
options.C: It prevents the puncture site from bruising
options.D: It is contaminated with dangerous skin bacteria

explanation: That initial droplet usually mixes with clear tissue fluid from the skin poke, which throws off the glucose reading. Wiping it away gives you a true blood sample!

question: What causes dizziness when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back?

options.A: An acute drop in blood glucose levels caused by the fetus
options.B: Reduced venous return caused by uterine compression of the vena cava
options.C: Sudden dehydration from excessive sweating during sleep
options.D: Spasms of the cerebral arteries due to high progesterone

explanation: Spot on! The heavy womb presses on the big vein (vena cava), slowing blood return to the heart and making her feel dizzy.

question: A patient has extremely dry, thick skin on their heels and soft, hydrated skin on their inner arm. Where will a topical cream absorb the fastest?

options.A: On the heel because it has more subcutaneous fat
options.B: On the inner arm because the skin is soft and hydrated
options.C: Absorption rate will be identical in both locations
options.D: On the heel because thick skin holds more medication

explanation: Hydrated skin and thinner skin barriers allow topical agents to penetrate much faster than dry, thick areas like the heels. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h2)

question: What physical characteristic indicates that a vein is a poor choice for cannulation?

options.A: The vein bounces back softly when pressed
options.B: The vein is clearly visible under light skin
options.C: The vein feels hard, rigid, and cord-like
options.D: The vein disappears temporarily when warmed

explanation: Hard or sclerosed veins are damaged and fragile, meaning they will easily rupture or fail to hold a cannula. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which type of validity checks if a test covers all the topics you were actually taught in class?

options.A: Clinical validity
options.B: Surface validity
options.C: Predictive validity
options.D: Content validity

explanation: Content validity ensures the exam questions actually match the course content you studied, so there are no unfair surprises.

question: In the popular BUBBLE-EE postpartum assessment guide, what does the second 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bonding
options.B: Bleeding
options.C: Bladder
options.D: Bowel

explanation: Remember the checklist: Breasts, Uterus, Bowel, Bladder, Lochia, Episiotomy, Extremities, and Emotions. You'll master this assessment in no time!

question: When giving a bed bath, in what direction should you wash the skin?

options.A: From the feet up to the face
options.B: From dirtiest areas to cleanest areas
options.C: From the left side to the right side
options.D: From cleanest areas to dirtier areas

explanation: Brilliant! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you don't drag germs from lower areas up onto sensitive spots like the face.

question: Why is the sequence of techniques changed when examining the abdomen?

options.A: Auscultation is done first so pressing on the belly does not change bowel sounds
options.B: Percussion is omitted entirely to prevent patient discomfort
options.C: Inspection is skipped because visual data is unreliable
options.D: Palpation must be done first to locate hidden organs before listening

explanation: Touching or pressing the abdomen can stimulate bowel activity, giving a false impression of bowel sounds. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h6)

question: What does 'somnolence' mean when we compare it to general fatigue?

options.A: An overwhelming urge to sleep and excessive drowsiness
options.B: Sudden paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.C: A complete lack of emotional feelings
options.D: Pain localized strictly in the peripheral joints

explanation: Spot on! While fatigue is about lacking energy to do things, somnolence is specifically that heavy, drooping-eyelids feeling where you just want to drift off to sleep.

question: Why is general inspection a great first step before doing a physical exam on a patient with a blood disorder?

options.A: It provides a quick way to measure the exact red blood cell count
options.B: It replaces the need to check laboratory blood test results completely
options.C: It is the only legal way to diagnose leukemia in the ward
options.D: It helps spot immediate signs of distress, fatigue, and distress clues

explanation: Looking at your patient first gives you a quick overall picture of their energy level, comfort, and obvious physical symptoms before you dive into detailed touching and listening.

question: What is the best way to care for a newborn baby's umbilical cord stump?

options.A: Applying strong iodine and native oils daily
options.B: Keeping it clean and dry without applying harsh substances
options.C: Covering it tightly with a waterproof plastic bandage
options.D: Washing it with medicated soap every single hour

explanation: Keep shining! Dry cord care is the gold standard—just keep it clean and dry and let it fall off naturally without putting oils or chemicals on it.

question: Why might a traumatized patient complain of chest tightness and nausea even when all their medical tests are normal?

options.A: The patient is intentionally trying to fake their injuries
options.B: A delayed infection is spreading through the bloodstream
options.C: Somatization translates emotional stress into physical symptoms
options.D: Standard hospital diagnostic machines are malfunctioning

explanation: Exactly! The mind and body are deeply connected. Emotional distress can show up as very real physical feelings like upset stomachs or tight chests—this is called somatization.

question: What makes an auto-disable (AD) syringe special?

options.A: It locks or breaks after a single use to prevent reuse
options.B: It changes color when exposed to direct sunlight
options.C: It can be sterilized in boiling water up to ten times
options.D: It has a detachable needle that can be safely recapped

explanation: Correct! AD syringes jam or break right after the first injection so nobody can accidentally reuse them on another patient.

question: Which activity is a great example of 'organizing' on a clinical ward?

options.A: Disciplining a staff member for arriving late
options.B: Ensuring dressing carts are fully stocked and placed near patient rooms
options.C: Deciding the long-term budget goals for the hospital
options.D: Giving a motivational speech during morning handover

explanation: Stocking and positioning your gear ahead of time is classic organizing that makes clinical work a breeze.

question: A patient suddenly feels intense terror, chest pain, and a sense of doom that peaks within minutes. What condition matches this?

options.A: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.B: Social anxiety disorder
options.C: Specific phobia
options.D: Panic disorder

explanation: Exactly! Those sudden, terrifying rushes with strong physical signs are classic hallmarks of panic attacks seen in panic disorder.

question: A child who quickly masters tough math concepts and deep thinking is showing signs of what?

options.A: Psychomotor ability
options.B: Creative productivity
options.C: Behavioral maturity
options.D: Intellectual giftedness

explanation: Spot on! Learning fast and reasoning deeply are classic signs of general intellectual giftedness rather than just a narrow skill. You're doing great!

question: What mask must you wear when entering a room under droplet precautions?

options.A: Double sterile surgical gloves
options.B: A full body hazardous materials suit
options.C: A fitted N95 respirator mask
options.D: A standard surgical or medical mask

explanation: Correct! A simple surgical mask does a great job blocking those heavy respiratory droplets from landing in your nose and mouth.

question: Why is it so helpful to note the exact pattern and layout of skin lesions?

options.A: It helps identify specific disease patterns and tracks treatment response
options.B: It proves that secondary lesions always turn into primary lesions
options.C: It eliminates the need to record vital signs during the shift
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will stop scratching immediately

explanation: Many skin conditions have a signature look or layout. Spotting this pattern makes it much easier to figure out what's wrong and if the treatment is working!

question: Besides giving us shape, what important minerals do our bones store for the body?

options.A: Calcium and phosphorus
options.B: Iron and magnesium
options.C: Sodium and chloride
options.D: Potassium and zinc

explanation: Think of your bones as a savings bank! They store vital minerals like calcium and phosphorus, releasing them into your bloodstream whenever your body needs a top-up.

question: As a nurse, why should you explore a patient's cultural practices rather than just banning them?

options.A: Traditional practices replace the need for all modern antibiotic treatments
options.B: Patients are more likely to ignore advice that completely dismisses their traditional beliefs
options.C: Cultural practices are always scientifically proven to be beneficial for health
options.D: Hospital policies legally require nurses to perform traditional steam baths

explanation: Spot on! When we respect our patients' beliefs instead of judging them, they trust us more and are way more likely to listen to our health advice.

question: What is the main reason a nurse schedules serial ultrasounds for a pregnant client with sickle cell disease?

options.A: To check if the maternal pelvis is widening properly
options.B: To measure the exact volume of maternal amniotic fluid daily
options.C: To determine the exact genetic subtype of the fetus
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for fetal anemia

explanation: You're doing great! Regular scans help us check how well the baby is growing and keep an eye out for fetal anemia.

question: Why is it so tricky to diagnose Lassa fever early just by looking at symptoms?

options.A: Patients rarely present with any fever during the first week
options.B: Its early symptoms closely resemble malaria and typhoid fever
options.C: Skin rashes appear immediately to confuse the clinician
options.D: Laboratory tests are always positive within the first two hours

explanation: Fever, headache, and body weakness happen with many tropical illnesses, which is why taking a careful travel and exposure history is so important.

question: Under the WHO medical rules, what does a Category 4 classification mean for a contraceptive method?

options.A: The benefits outweigh the risks in most cases
options.B: There are no restrictions on using the method
options.C: The method can be used with routine monitoring
options.D: The method represents an unacceptable health risk

explanation: Category 4 means 'Stop!' — the condition is too dangerous, and the contraceptive must not be used because it puts the client's health at serious risk.

question: What is the main job of cortisol during the stress response?

options.A: To lower blood pressure and slow down breathing
options.B: To enhance immune system activity and fight infection
options.C: To raise blood glucose and supply energy to vital organs
options.D: To stimulate digestion and nutrient absorption

explanation: Cortisol acts like an emergency power switch, boosting your blood sugar so your brain and muscles have the immediate fuel they need to react.

question: What is a crucial teaching point for someone prescribed an epinephrine auto-injector for severe allergies?

options.A: Keep the device stored inside a kitchen refrigerator at all times
options.B: Demonstrate how to self-administer the device into the outer thigh and call emergency services
options.C: Use the auto-injector only after taking oral antihistamines first
options.D: Replace the device once every ten years regardless of expiration date

explanation: Make sure your patient knows how to jab that auto-injector firmly into their outer thigh, and remind them to always call for emergency help right after!

question: Which germ is commonly linked to undercooked poultry and raw eggs?

options.A: Streptococcus
options.B: Lactobacillus
options.C: Aspergillus
options.D: Salmonella

explanation: Great job! Salmonella loves hanging out in raw poultry and eggs. Proper cooking kills it right away. You're doing brilliantly!

question: What is the main problem in the body when someone has anaemia?

options.A: Increased thickness of the blood plasma
options.B: Rapid destruction of blood platelets
options.C: Too many white blood cells
options.D: Reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood

explanation: You've got this! Anaemia simply means the blood doesn't have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to carry the oxygen your body needs to function well.

question: Why do doctors often choose laparoscopy instead of traditional open surgery?

options.A: It guarantees zero risk of post-operative complications
options.B: It causes less pain and allows a faster recovery
options.C: It requires no special surgical equipment or training
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for general anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Because the cuts (incisions) are very small, there is less damage to the body, less pain afterwards, and the patient gets back on their feet much quicker.

question: Which pregnancy hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing the valve between the stomach and food pipe?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body to make room for baby, which also loosens the sphincter keeping stomach acid down.

question: Which of these actions breaks the rule of current, truthful documentation?

options.A: Updating the care plan after assessing a new wound
options.B: Charting routine morning vital signs before taking them
options.C: Writing a note ten minutes after giving an injection
options.D: Recording a patient's reaction right after a procedure

explanation: Spot on! Charting care before you actually do it is falsification and is dangerous and illegal.

question: When assessing muscle strength, how should the nurse evaluate the limbs?

options.A: By measuring the exact circumference with a tape
options.B: Bilaterally to compare both sides of the body
options.C: Only after administering pain medication
options.D: Only on the dominant side to save time

explanation: Comparing opposite sides helps identify localized weakness or asymmetry caused by neurological injury. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h6)

question: What equipment do you attach directly to an oxygen source to control how fast the gas flows?

options.A: Pressure gauge
options.B: Pulse oximeter
options.C: Flow meter
options.D: Humidifier bottle

explanation: The flow meter is your best friend for control—it lets you accurately dial in the exact liters per minute prescribed for your patient.

question: What do we call it when blood collects inside the pleural space?

options.A: Pneumothorax
options.B: Empyema
options.C: Hemothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: You got it! 'Hemo' means blood and 'thorax' means chest, so blood in the chest cavity is a hemothorax.

question: What is the main goal of grouping drugs into pharmacological classes?

options.A: To determine the exact retail cost of prescription drugs
options.B: To establish the legal expiration date for various drug classes
options.C: To identify which pharmaceutical company manufactured the medicine
options.D: To group medications based on their mechanism and physiological effects

explanation: Grouping drugs by how they work in the body helps you easily predict their actions and safety profiles without memorizing every single pill!

question: Why must nurses stress to parents the importance of finishing a child's entire course of antibiotics?

options.A: To prevent the child from developing a skin rash
options.B: To permanently boost the child's daily appetite
options.C: To completely wipe out the bacteria and prevent relapse
options.D: To ensure the child gains healthy weight rapidly

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early just because the child 'looks better' can let hidden bacteria bounce back and cause more kidney damage. Patient education at its finest!

question: Why should nurses worry when a patient has severe, ongoing itching?

options.A: It proves that the topical medication is working effectively
options.B: It always indicates that a patient has systemic kidney failure
options.C: Scratching breaks the skin barrier and increases infection risk
options.D: It prevents the formation of primary lesions like macules

explanation: The itch-scratch cycle damages the skin's natural defense shield, making it super easy for germs and bacteria to get in.

question: What is the best way for a community health nurse to address cultural beliefs that support FGM?

options.A: Agreeing that the traditional practice is beneficial for girls
options.B: Engaging community leaders respectfully while educating them on health risks
options.C: Arresting family members immediately without talking to them
options.D: Ignoring the cultural practice and focusing only on hospital management

explanation: Well done! Lasting change happens when we work hand-in-hand with trusted community and religious leaders through open, respectful dialogue.

question: Why is checking a patient's medications a key part of preventing falls?

options.A: Medications are the only known cause of falls in the elderly
options.B: Pharmacists require routine checks to maintain their licenses
options.C: Older adults always take too many vitamins instead of real food
options.D: Many common drugs cause dizziness, sedation, or balance issues

explanation: Spot on! Blood pressure pills and sleeping meds can make a patient dizzy or lightheaded, leading to accidental falls.

question: Why do advanced tumors often become resistant to medical treatments like chemotherapy?

options.A: The body's immune system destroys the medication before it reaches the tumor
options.B: Chemotherapy drugs turn normal cells into malignant cancer cells
options.C: Genetic diversity creates varied cell populations with different drug resistance traits
options.D: Tumor cells develop a protective bone shell that blocks all medications

explanation: As mutations accumulate, cancer cells become diverse; while some cells die from treatment, resistant clones survive and multiply. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h5)

question: In diastolic heart failure, what is the main problem with how the heart works?

options.A: The electrical system fires at a very irregular rhythm
options.B: The heart muscle cannot relax and fill with blood properly
options.C: The heart muscle cannot squeeze hard enough to push blood out
options.D: The heart valves fail to open during pumping

explanation: In diastolic failure, the heart muscle gets stiff. It can squeeze okay, but it struggles to relax and fill up with enough blood first.

question: Why is genetic testing especially important when checking for Huntington's disease?

options.A: It replaces the need for a physical neurological exam
options.B: It measures the exact level of dopamine in the blood
options.C: It immediately stops the progression of the disease
options.D: It proves the patient has a specific inherited gene mutation

explanation: Huntington's disease runs in families. Genetic tests can spot the exact inherited gene mutation responsible for it. Every question you answer makes your future clinical shifts easier!

question: What is a crucial safety rule when caring for a patient in skeletal traction?

options.A: The patient's body weight must rest entirely on the traction pulleys
options.B: The hanging weights must remain completely unobstructed and free
options.C: The traction ropes should rest firmly against the bed frame
options.D: The weights should be placed on the floor to reduce tension

explanation: Those weights need to dangle freely in the air! If they touch the floor or bed, the pulling force stops working properly.

question: A patient insists on an IV infusion at a private pharmacy because they paid cash and want visible treatment. What factor is primarily at play here?

options.A: Financial incentives and consumer perception of value
options.B: Strict adherence to evidence-based clinical guidelines
options.C: An acute emergency requiring immediate fluid resuscitation
options.D: Standard protocol for managing mild upper respiratory infections

explanation: Both the provider's financial motive and the patient's desire for visible proof of care contribute to unnecessary treatments. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h4)

question: When is a nurse most likely to consider using the rectal route for a patient?

options.A: When the patient prefers a fast topical skin effect
options.B: When the patient needs a daily multivitamin tablet
options.C: When the patient cannot take medications by mouth
options.D: When the patient has a mild headache and can swallow

explanation: If oral intake is blocked due to vomiting, unconsciousness, or swallowing difficulties, the rectal route serves as a practical alternative. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which type of medicine is commonly given to prevent blood clots in patients with peripheral arterial disease?

options.A: Water pills (diuretics) that save potassium
options.B: Heart-stimulating drugs
options.C: Inhaled medicines for the lungs
options.D: Antiplatelet drugs like aspirin

explanation: Antiplatelet medications keep tiny blood cells (platelets) from sticking together on rough fatty plaques, helping to stop clots before they form.

question: Which screening tool is commonly used to check for delirium in ventilated ICU patients?

options.A: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.B: Apgar Score
options.C: CAM-ICU
options.D: Braden Scale

explanation: The CAM-ICU (Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU) is specifically built to help us catch delirium even when patients can't talk.

question: What is the primary goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants
options.B: To provide free medications for all childhood illnesses
options.C: To increase the birth rate across rural populations
options.D: To ensure healthy pregnancies and safe deliveries for all women

explanation: Safe motherhood initiatives focus specifically on protecting the health and well-being of mothers throughout pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal period. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h1)

question: How should you position your patient's head during an eye wash?

options.A: Tilted slightly toward the affected side
options.B: Tilted firmly toward the unaffected side
options.C: Positioned flat and facing straight up
options.D: Tilted backward as far as the neck allows

explanation: Tilting toward the bad side ensures the dirty runoff flows away off the face instead of spilling into the healthy eye.

question: What is the main sign of a structural congenital anomaly?

options.A: A physical malformation or missing body part
options.B: A chemical imbalance in the blood
options.C: A delayed reaction to sound
options.D: An inability to make red blood cells

explanation: Think 'structure' equals 'shape' or 'form'. Structural anomalies are physical defects you can usually see or feel on the body.

question: What is a major focus of infection control education during community health nursing outreach?

options.A: Encouraging residents to avoid visiting local healthcare clinics
options.B: Training villagers to perform complex surgical procedures at home
options.C: Teaching families practical hygiene habits and safe home care for sick relatives
options.D: Promoting the purchase of expensive hospital-grade air purifiers

explanation: Community nursing focuses on empowering families with simple, low-cost habits that prevent disease transmission at home. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)

question: Which simple task can you encourage a relative to do to help them feel involved in patient care?

options.A: Adjusting intravenous medication flow rates
options.B: Reading complex laboratory blood test results
options.C: Administering prescribed narcotic injections
options.D: Moistening the patient's dry lips and skin

explanation: Small comforts like moistening lips give family members a wonderful, safe way to care for their loved one and feel useful.

question: A patient experiencing severe shortness of breath is unlikely to focus on which type of need at that moment?

options.A: Getting enough oxygen into the lungs
options.B: Achieving personal growth and self-actualization
options.C: Maintaining basic fluid balance
options.D: Relieving physical pain

explanation: Until basic physiological survival needs like breathing are met, higher-level needs such as self-actualization take a back seat. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a common emotional response a patient might experience after an abortion?

options.A: An immediate desire to write a public memoir about the event
options.B: Complete emotional numbness that lasts for an entire lifetime
options.C: A wide range of feelings including relief, grief, or anxiety
options.D: Permanent clinical detachment from all family members

explanation: Exactly! Feelings after pregnancy loss are deeply personal and can span anywhere from sadness and anxiety to relief.

question: What happens when you mix two bases that don't go together?

options.A: The mixture separates and delivers an uneven dose
options.B: The mixture instantly cures all skin infections
options.C: The chemical formula permanently turns into a solid block
options.D: The active medication becomes twice as strong

explanation: If bases don't match, they split apart, meaning some parts of the cream will have too much drug and others too little. You've got this!

question: What is the medical name for normal earwax?

options.A: Mucin
options.B: Tympanum
options.C: Cerumen
options.D: Sebum

explanation: Cerumen is just the fancy medical word for the natural wax our ears make to keep things clean and protected. You've got this!

question: Why might a speech-language pathologist recommend thickened liquids for a patient with a degenerative condition?

options.A: To increase the patient's daily caloric and protein intake
options.B: To cure the underlying inflammation in the throat muscles
options.C: To make the drink taste more appealing to the patient
options.D: To prevent the liquid from moving too fast and causing aspiration

explanation: Thickened liquids move slower down the throat, giving weakened swallowing muscles more time to close the airway and prevent choking. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h6)

question: What is the main objective of the empowerment approach in health promotion?

options.A: Ensuring that government officials make all health decisions for citizens
options.B: Forcing communities to build modern hospitals using their own unpaid labor
options.C: Helping people gain the confidence and skills to take control of their own health
options.D: Relying solely on foreign pharmaceutical donations

explanation: Empowerment focuses on building self-reliance so communities can advocate for their own needs and solve local health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: A child weighs 20 kg. The safe dose is 5 mg/kg/day. What is the total daily dose?

options.A: 4 mg
options.B: 100 mg
options.C: 25 mg
options.D: 200 mg

explanation: Multiply weight by the dose per kg: 20 kg × 5 mg = 100 mg daily. You've got this math down!

question: Why must nurses check for other physical symptoms alongside pain during a palliative assessment?

options.A: Multiple symptoms interact and can make each other worse, like breathlessness causing panic
options.B: Non-pain symptoms are usually much more dangerous than actual physical pain
options.C: Insurance companies only pay for care if three symptoms are treated at once
options.D: Doctors only look at pain scores and ignore all other bodily complaints

explanation: Symptoms don't happen in isolation. Struggling to breathe can trigger panic, so we need to look at the whole picture!

question: What is the main reason conflict happens in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Having too many registered nurses on a single ward
options.B: Working an excessive number of consecutive night shifts
options.C: Strict adherence to hospital operational policies
options.D: A clash of values, goals, or needs between people

explanation: Conflict simply pops up when people interact and their personal values, goals, or needs don't match up. It happens to everyone, even the best healthcare teams!

question: Why is it important to establish large-bore intravenous lines for a patient with severe haemorrhage?

options.A: To deliver pain medication straight to the heart
options.B: To prevent the veins from collapsing permanently
options.C: To allow rapid infusion of fluids and blood products
options.D: To make it easier to draw blood for daily lab tests

explanation: Large intravenous catheters allow fluids and blood to be pushed into the circulation quickly to restore lost volume. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h6)

question: What happens if someone's visual association area is damaged, but their primary visual cortex is completely fine?

options.A: They lose the ability to move their eyes from side to side
options.B: They can see shapes and light but cannot recognize what objects are
options.C: They can no longer feel textures or temperatures with their hands
options.D: They become completely blind and cannot perceive any light at all

explanation: Great question! Their eyes and primary cortex still capture the picture just fine, but the association area can't process the meaning—so they see things without knowing what they're looking at.

question: Why must nurses tailor assessment tools to fit a degenerative patient's physical limits?

options.A: To make the test results legally binding in a court of law
options.B: To eliminate the need for family members to be present
options.C: To ensure the patient does not get tired or frustrated during testing
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing paper questionnaires

explanation: If a patient is exhausted, test scores won't show their true ability. Matching their energy levels keeps the assessment accurate and stress-free.

question: What is polypharmacy?

options.A: The practice of buying fake drugs from unlicensed local market vendors
options.B: The manufacturing of herbal remedies without standard quality control
options.C: The storage of expired pharmaceutical products in hospital pharmacy stores
options.D: The simultaneous use of multiple medications by a single patient

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to a patient taking multiple medications concurrently, which raises the risk of drug interactions. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h3)

question: Why do normal lab test values change when a woman is pregnant?

options.A: Pregnant women have a slower metabolic rate overall
options.B: Blood cells shrink in size during the first trimester
options.C: The laboratory equipment is calibrated differently for women
options.D: Pregnancy hormones significantly alter baseline body chemistry

explanation: Think of pregnancy as a total body makeover! Because hormones shift so much, the normal lab ranges you use for non-pregnant patients simply don't apply here.

question: During which phase of adolescence do teenagers really start thinking deeply and caring a lot about what their friends think?

options.A: Late adolescence
options.B: Early adolescence
options.C: Middle adolescence
options.D: Infancy transition

explanation: Middle adolescence is when deep peer loyalty kicks in and teenagers start exploring more abstract, big-picture thinking.

question: What is the main purpose of development committees in Nigerian primary health care?

options.A: To replace trained doctors in rural clinics
options.B: To encourage community participation and local ownership
options.C: To collect taxes for hospital construction
options.D: To manage federal medical centers directly

explanation: These committees exist to involve local people so they can take charge of their own health needs and partner effectively with health workers. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is it important to let the nurse share their side of the story during an investigation?

options.A: To ensure fairness and uncover any misunderstood details
options.B: To trick the nurse into admitting a bigger crime
options.C: To let the nurse write the final company policies
options.D: To delay the disciplinary process indefinitely

explanation: Listening to the employee provides a complete picture, ensuring management does not act on incomplete information. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h6)

question: What is the name of the natural pacemaker that sets the rhythm for the heart?

options.A: Purkinje fiber
options.B: Bundle of His
options.C: Atrioventricular node
options.D: Sinoatrial node

explanation: The Sinoatrial (SA) node is the boss of heart rhythms! It fires off electrical signals the fastest, keeping the whole heart beating in a steady, regular pattern.

question: What term describes the deep emotional exhaustion nurses feel from caring for suffering patients over time?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Compassion fatigue
options.C: Cognitive dissonance
options.D: Disenfranchised loss

explanation: Spot on! Compassion fatigue is real in nursing. It happens when you pour so much care into others without taking time to recharge your own batteries.

question: Why are elderly adults usually more at risk for catching infections?

options.A: Their skin becomes completely impermeable
options.B: Their immune defenses decline with age
options.C: They consume too many hospital medications
options.D: They have faster cellular regeneration

explanation: As people age, the immune system naturally slows down a bit, making it easier for germs to take hold. Great job thinking about your patients' vulnerability!

question: Which of these is a BAD habit when trying to stop the spread of a respiratory infection?

options.A: Coughing into the inside of your elbow
options.B: Proper disposal of used paper tissues
options.C: Frequent hand washing with soap and water
options.D: Sharing drinking cups with others

explanation: You got it! Sharing cups or spoons transfers saliva and germs straight to others, spreading the infection around.

question: What is the main job of sodium fluoride inside the blood collection tube?

options.A: It stains white blood cells for the microscope
options.B: It speeds up blood clotting so serum separates instantly
options.C: It stops blood cells from consuming the glucose inside the tube
options.D: It stops the blood sample from freezing during transport

explanation: Think of sodium fluoride as a preservative. Without it, the living blood cells inside the tube would keep eating up the glucose, giving you a falsely low lab result!

question: Why are elderly patients much more prone to skin tears?

options.A: Their skin cells regenerate at an unusually rapid pace
options.B: Their blood circulation is much faster than in younger adults
options.C: Their epidermis thins and subcutaneous fat decreases
options.D: Their sweat glands produce excessive amounts of natural oils

explanation: Well done! As people age, their skin naturally thins out and loses its soft padding, making it much more delicate.

question: Which main artery supplies blood directly to the uterus?

options.A: Brachial artery
options.B: Uterine artery
options.C: Renal artery
options.D: Femoral artery

explanation: The uterine artery, branching from the internal iliac artery, brings oxygen-rich blood directly to the uterine walls. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why is creating a confidential and non-judgmental environment crucial when discussing sexual health?

options.A: It guarantees that no chronic illness will ever develop
options.B: It encourages patients to share sensitive concerns and seek help early
options.C: It prevents patients from ever asking questions about medications
options.D: It is required by law to prescribe over-the-counter vitamins

explanation: Patients will only confide intimate struggles if they trust their nurse will treat them with respect and absolute privacy. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h8)

question: What is the golden rule when conducting a home visit for a family planning defaulter?

options.A: Announce the client's medical history loudly to all neighbors
options.B: Maintain strict confidentiality and protect client privacy
options.C: Bring local community leaders to witness the counseling session
options.D: Leave written flyers on the front door for everyone to read

explanation: Privacy is vital! Protecting the client's medical information keeps them safe from community gossip or partner backlash.

question: As a nurse, what is the most important first step when caring for a pregnant teenager?

options.A: Isolating her from her family members
options.B: Putting her on strict dietary restriction
options.C: Reporting her immediately to child welfare authorities
options.D: Building a trusting, non-judgmental therapeutic relationship

explanation: Spot on! Teens are often afraid of being scolded. Building trust makes them feel safe to come to the clinic and share what they need.

question: A nurse is teaching a rural community about cholera prevention. Which approach will work best?

options.A: Insisting that villagers change their ancient cultural practices without any explanation
options.B: Handing out complex scientific research journals written in advanced medical terminology
options.C: Waiting until an outbreak kills several people before holding a public meeting
options.D: Using local languages and culturally relevant examples to explain safe drinking water habits

explanation: Spot on! Keeping health education simple, friendly, and in the local language ensures everyone understands and can easily protect themselves.

question: In the chain of infection, what is the main job of an infective host?

options.A: To act exclusively as a dead-end for microbial life
options.B: To harbor an infectious agent and serve as a source of infection
options.C: To manufacture antibodies for community protection
options.D: To destroy invading pathogens before symptoms appear

explanation: You've got this! Think of the host as a comfortable home for the germ. It gives the pathogen a place to stay and acts as the starting point for spreading to others.

question: Which of these features is typically seen in a female pelvis rather than a male pelvis?

options.A: A wide pubic arch
options.B: A deep, narrow cavity
options.C: Inward-projecting ischial spines
options.D: A heart-shaped pelvic inlet

explanation: Women have a nice wide pubic arch to help make room for a baby to pass through easily.

question: How can excessive moisture and high temperatures affect the normal vaginal environment?

options.A: By stimulating excessive production of protective estrogen hormones
options.B: By altering the normal pH balance and encouraging harmful microbial overgrowth
options.C: By completely sterilizing the vaginal canal of all bacteria forever
options.D: By permanently destroying the anatomical structure of the cervix

explanation: Think of the vagina as having a delicate, natural balance. Too much heat and moisture can upset that pH balance, making it easier for bad bacteria or yeast to grow.

question: Why can suddenly stopping long-term steroid medications trigger an adrenal crisis?

options.A: Stopping steroids causes the liver to destroy all circulating glucose
options.B: Steroid pills turn into toxic acid inside the stomach lining
options.C: The adrenal glands become lazy and stop making natural cortisol
options.D: The thyroid gland reacts by shutting down body temperature controls

explanation: When you take external steroids for a long time, your adrenals take a break from making their own. If you stop abruptly, they can't bounce back fast enough!

question: How should a nurse figure out how much pain a patient is feeling?

options.A: By guessing based on the size of the tumor visible on scans
options.B: By checking how much medication the doctor prescribed
options.C: By measuring changes in the patient's blood pressure and pulse
options.D: By believing the patient's own report of their pain

explanation: Always trust your patient! Pain is a personal experience, and how they say they feel is the most reliable guide we have.

question: When can palliative care start for someone diagnosed with cancer?

options.A: At the time of diagnosis alongside curative treatment
options.B: Only when all chemotherapy and radiation have failed
options.C: Strictly during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.D: Only after the patient is discharged to hospice care

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the end of life—it can start right away to help manage symptoms and keep the patient comfortable while fighting the disease.

question: A patient admitted for severe hyperemesis is about to receive IV glucose fluids. Why must she receive thiamine (Vitamin B1) first?

options.A: To help the liver process the incoming sugar more quickly
options.B: To prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy from vitamin deficiency
options.C: To prevent allergic reactions to the plastic IV tubing
options.D: To stop the patient from feeling sleepy during the infusion

explanation: Great catch! Giving sugar to a malnourished patient without thiamine can trigger a serious brain complication called Wernicke's encephalopathy. Always protect the brain first!

question: What is the main purpose of wearing a personal dosimeter badge in a radiology department?

options.A: To prove to patients that the diagnostic equipment is clean
options.B: To block radioactive waves from entering the nurse's chest
options.C: To grant the nurse emergency access to locked X-ray rooms
options.D: To measure the accumulated amount of radiation exposure over time

explanation: Dosimeter badges record occupational radiation doses, alerting staff if their exposure levels begin to approach unsafe limits. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h6)

question: Your stroke patient has left-sided neglect. Where should you place their lunch tray?

options.A: Place the tray directly in the center without mentioning its location
options.B: Encourage the client to reach across their body to the left side
options.C: Place all food items and utensils on the client's right side
options.D: Feed the client entirely to avoid any missed food or frustration

explanation: Putting everything on their strong, unaffected right side makes sure they can actually see their food and eat independently, keeping them well-nourished and happy.

question: What are the three core components of the standard Post-Abortion Care (PAC) model?

options.A: Surgical sterilization, mandatory psychiatric evaluation, and legal reporting
options.B: Emergency treatment, family planning counseling, and reproductive health linkage
options.C: Antenatal booking, nutritional rehabilitation, and infant immunization
options.D: Blood transfusion, long-term hospitalization, and vocational training

explanation: PAC is a complete package: treat the immediate emergency, talk about family planning so it doesn't happen again, and connect the patient to ongoing health care. You'll see this model everywhere in public health!

question: Why are birth control pills often given to a patient with functional ovarian cysts?

options.A: To cure any underlying bacterial pelvic infections
options.B: To suppress ovulation and prevent new cysts from forming
options.C: To permanently increase the production of progesterone
options.D: To instantly dissolve and shrink existing large cysts

explanation: By stopping ovulation, hormonal pills cut off the root cause of functional cysts, giving the ovaries a nice little break.

question: How can a nurse best help a quiet 16-year-old feel comfortable sharing her health history?

options.A: Demand immediate answers before starting the physical exam
options.B: Read medical terminology directly from the textbook
options.C: Use open-ended questions and an empathetic tone
options.D: Speak exclusively to the accompanying friend instead

explanation: Open-ended questions and a warm tone help lower anxiety and make the patient feel respected.

question: What makes true sexual consent valid?

options.A: Financial approval from the local community leader
options.B: Written permission signed by both set of parents
options.C: The freedom to say no without negative consequences
options.D: Physical dominance by one partner over the other

explanation: You got it! Consent must always be a free and willing choice, without any force, threats, or pressure.

question: A stroke patient has weak muscles and needs a little bit of help to move their arm fully. What exercise is best?

options.A: Active-assistive exercises
options.B: Passive range of motion
options.C: Complete bed rest restriction
options.D: Heavy weightlifting resistance

explanation: Teamwork! The patient does as much as they can, and you help finish the movement. That is active-assistive exercise.

question: What happens when the chemical signals that control normal cell division break down?

options.A: Cells transform into normal bone
options.B: Cells multiply uncontrollably
options.C: Cells stop dividing permanently
options.D: Cells immediately shrink and die

explanation: Spot on! When the body's natural brakes on the cell cycle fail, cells lose their stop signals and keep dividing, leading to abnormal growth.

question: Why is it important to talk about pain management before the patient takes misoprostol?

options.A: Pain medications must be taken to prevent allergic reactions to the drug
options.B: Analgesics speed up the absorption of the hormone in the stomach lining
options.C: Misoprostol causes strong uterine contractions that lead to significant cramping
options.D: Pain medication stops the excessive bleeding that occurs right away

explanation: Cramping is a very normal part of the process because the uterus is working hard to empty. Planning ahead for pain relief keeps our patients comfortable!

question: What is a key prevention message nurses should teach families to stop Lassa fever at home?

options.A: Keep doors and windows wide open during the evening hours
options.B: Dry all harvested grains directly on bare soil surfaces
options.C: Store food items in tightly sealed, rodent-proof containers
options.D: Keep pet cats away from all residential cooking areas

explanation: Locking up food in secure containers keeps rats away and stops them from contaminating your grains with urine and faeces.

question: How does immunotherapy work differently from standard chemotherapy?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any diagnostic imaging procedures.
options.B: It only acts on the outer layer of the skin and never reaches the lungs.
options.C: It freezes the tumor tissue by lowering the core body temperature.
options.D: It empowers the body's own immune defenses to target and destroy cancer cells.

explanation: Exactly right! Instead of just attacking cells directly like chemo, immunotherapy helps your own white blood cells recognize and fight off the cancer.

question: What is the main risk of failing to regularly check expiration dates on kit supplies?

options.A: Using expired items that may be ineffective or unsafe for patients
options.B: Changing the color of the bag's inner lining
options.C: Attracting household insects to the storage locker
options.D: Making the visiting bag too heavy to carry comfortably

explanation: Expired antiseptics or sterile materials can lose their potency or harbor contamination, endangering patient safety. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h6)

question: Which structures should you palpate when doing a routine male genital check?

options.A: Testes and epididymis
options.B: Bulbourethral glands only
options.C: Ureters and renal pelvis
options.D: Seminal vesicles and bladder

explanation: You got it! Gently checking the testes and the epididymis helps you spot any lumps, swelling, or tenderness early on.

question: What tough protein gives the outer layer of our skin its strength?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Keratin

explanation: Great job! Keratin is a tough, fibrous protein that makes our outer skin cells strong and durable. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is a major threat to an older adult's emotional well-being?

options.A: An increase in free time and lack of daily responsibilities
options.B: Excessive physical strength and boundless energy
options.C: Cumulative life stressors and chronic physical pain
options.D: Having too many hobbies to choose from each day

explanation: Constant body pains and a heavy buildup of life losses can really weigh down an older person's spirit. You're doing great!

question: Why might a doctor choose a transjejunal feeding tube instead of a standard gastric tube?

options.A: To bypass the stomach entirely due to high aspiration risk
options.B: To provide a larger reservoir for liquid formula storage
options.C: To make daily stoma site cleaning much easier for caregivers
options.D: To allow the patient to chew and swallow food while feeding

explanation: Transjejunal tubes deliver nutrients further down into the small bowel, which helps prevent severe reflux and aspiration in vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is the patient told to hold their breath while the doctor inserts the needle?

options.A: To stop air from entering through the skin
options.B: To keep their blood pressure from dropping too low
options.C: To keep the diaphragm still so the liver doesn't get torn
options.D: To save oxygen in case they feel stressed

explanation: Correct! Holding the breath stops the chest and diaphragm from moving, keeping the liver completely still for a safe, clean needle entry.

question: What should you do immediately if a patient shows signs of pain while their arm is being moved?

options.A: Continue moving faster to get past the painful spot
options.B: Ask a relative to hold the arm down so you can finish
options.C: Stop the exercise right away and check the joint
options.D: Ignore it because passive exercise always hurts

explanation: Pain is your stop sign! It tells you something is being over-stretched or injured. Always pause and assess.

question: What was a major focus of early public health pioneers like Florence Nightingale?

options.A: Hospital financial management
options.B: Pharmaceutical drug manufacturing
options.C: Advanced neurosurgical procedures
options.D: Environmental sanitation and clean water

explanation: Spot on! Florence Nightingale and early leaders knew that clean water and basic hygiene were the true keys to stopping the spread of diseases.

question: What type of lubricant should you always use when inserting a rectal medication?

options.A: Petroleum-based grease
options.B: Cooking vegetable oil
options.C: Alcohol-based sanitizer
options.D: Water-soluble lubricant

explanation: Water-soluble lubricants help the suppository slide in smoothly without hurting delicate tissues or damaging gloves.

question: Lab results show a patient has large (macrocytic) red blood cells. Which vitamin shortage should you check for first?

options.A: Vitamin B12 or folate
options.B: Vitamin D and calcium
options.C: Iron and copper
options.D: Potassium and sodium

explanation: Spot on! Vitamins B12 and folate act like master builders for DNA during red blood cell growth. Without them, the cells grow too large instead of maturing properly.

question: Why do nurses keep doing frequent neuro checks for unstable patients?

options.A: To catch early signs of rising intracranial pressure
options.B: To ensure the patient stays awake all night long
options.C: To keep the patient's family members from worrying
options.D: To prevent the patient from asking too many questions

explanation: Things can change fast in acute care. Frequent checks help you catch warning signs of pressure in the brain early, way before serious damage happens.

question: How can a large youth population become a 'demographic dividend' instead of an economic strain?

options.A: By encouraging mass emigration of young people abroad
options.B: By ignoring youth unemployment until they reach retirement age
options.C: Through heavy investments in education, health, and job creation
options.D: By restricting all youths from participating in the labor market

explanation: When we invest in our youth through good schools, healthcare, and jobs, they turn into a superpower for the economy instead of facing unemployment struggles.

question: A pregnant patient at 28 weeks complains of severe heartburn after eating. What is the best advice to give her?

options.A: Lie flat on your back immediately after meals to rest your digestion
options.B: Take strong laxatives every evening to empty your bowels completely
options.C: Eat small, frequent meals and avoid lying down right after eating
options.D: Drink large glasses of water with every meal to dilute stomach acid

explanation: Smaller meals keep the stomach from getting overloaded, and staying upright uses gravity to keep the acid where it belongs!

question: What is a common early symptom of hypoglycemia that a nurse should teach a client to recognize?

options.A: Extreme sweet-smelling breath
options.B: Severe peripheral edema
options.C: Shakiness and sweating
options.D: Kussmaul breathing patterns

explanation: When blood sugar drops too low, the nervous system reacts quickly, causing tremors, sweating, anxiety, and heart palpitations. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h8)

question: Why is it usually best not to force extra fluids or IV drips on an actively dying patient?

options.A: It can cause fluid overload and painful swelling
options.B: It immediately speeds up the dying process
options.C: It causes severe throat infections
options.D: It completely stops the patient from feeling any pain

explanation: As the body systems slow down, they cannot process extra fluids well. This leads to swelling and congestion rather than helping the patient heal. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h3)

question: Why are the bones of the fetal skull separated by sutures and fontanelles during childbirth?

options.A: To prevent the cerebrospinal fluid from building up inside the cranial cavity
options.B: To allow the skull bones to overlap and change shape inside the pelvis
options.C: To protect the baby's brain from normal changes in maternal blood pressure
options.D: To provide extra room for rapid brain growth during the first stage of labour

explanation: The gaps in the skull allow the bones to shift and overlap, reducing the head's diameter so it can pass safely through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h1)

question: Which sign strongly suggests internal bleeding in a patient on blood thinners?

options.A: Complaints of severe itching on the arms and legs
options.B: A sudden rise in the patient's body temperature
options.C: An increase in urine output over twenty-four hours
options.D: The presence of dark, tarry stools in the bedpan

explanation: Dark, tarry stools are a classic warning sign of bleeding in the stomach or intestines. Spotting this early saves lives!

question: What is the best position for a patient during a standard lumbar puncture?

options.A: Sitting straight upright with arms down
options.B: Lateral fetal position
options.C: Prone face down on pillows
options.D: Flat on the back with legs straight

question: Why is personal integrity a must-have trait for a nurse leader?

options.A: It builds trust and ensures ethical standards are upheld under pressure
options.B: It guarantees the unit will never experience a budget shortfall
options.C: It allows the leader to override physician orders safely
options.D: It eliminates the need for written hospital policies

explanation: Integrity builds deep trust. When things get tough, an honest and principled leader keeps the team focused on doing the right thing for patients.

question: What happens to red blood cells during a sickle cell crisis?

options.A: Cells swell and burst open prematurely
options.B: Cells become rigid and crescent-shaped
options.C: Cells lose all of their surface proteins
options.D: Cells shrink into tiny spherical shapes

explanation: You've got this! Abnormal hemoglobin S changes the shape of the red blood cells, making them hard and crescent-shaped when they drop off oxygen.

question: Where is the best place on an infant's body to give an intramuscular (IM) vaccine?

options.A: Abdominal subcutaneous tissue
options.B: Deltoid muscle in the upper arm
options.C: Gluteus maximus muscle in the buttocks

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take immediately after discovering a patient has fallen?

question: What does the term 'nutrient density' mean?

question: What are the three core ingredients needed for valid informed consent?

question: Who is the best person to translate for a patient who doesn't speak English during a health history?

question: How do conflicts or humanitarian crises usually affect the rate of early marriages in affected areas?

question: Why might a patient with chronic pain need a higher dose of their pain medication after taking it for several months?

question: Which medication class is quickly given to calm down inflammation during a sudden MS flare-up?

question: What is the right nursing action when you spot rigid, overlapping skull bones on a newborn?

question: A mother calls the clinic because her child has a fever and a stiff neck. What advice should the nurse give?

question: What are diverticula?

question: Why is it important to use the correct blood pressure cuff size?

question: What long-term heart problem often develops from chronic, untreated severe anemia?

question: What is the correct technique for pulling out a peripheral IV catheter?

question: What is the primary goal of cancer screening programs?

question: What usually happens if a family planning client never returns for follow-up checks?

question: What happens to extra glucose when your body already has enough energy?

question: Why do resource-limited regions often report higher rates of patient harm?

question: What is the main purpose of achieving high community vaccination coverage?

question: What are standing orders in primary health care?

question: Why is keeping the head of a ventilated patient's bed elevated at 30 to 45 degrees such an important nursing action?

question: What makes a patient care goal both effective and useful?

question: What is the primary reason for keeping a functioning suction apparatus nearby during a gastric lavage setup?
