options.D: It disappears completely within a few days without treatment

explanation: 'Transmural' simply means it goes all the way through—digging deep from the mucosa right across the muscle layers!

question: Which print material is best to hang on a busy clinic waiting room wall to grab quick attention?

options.A: Posters
options.B: Textbooks
options.C: Logbooks
options.D: Brochures

explanation: Posters are large and eye-catching, making them perfect for high-traffic walls where patients can quickly glance at them while waiting.

question: What is the main purpose of the initial evaluation phase in rehabilitation?

options.A: Discharging the patient permanently to their home
options.B: Identifying baseline functional deficits and recovery potential
options.C: Initiating high-impact athletic training
options.D: Stopping all medications to test natural healing

explanation: Before planning treatment, the team checks what the patient can and cannot do yet so they can build a personalized recovery plan.

question: What is the most important nursing action when a patient talks about active thoughts of suicide?

options.A: Wait until the next scheduled clinic visit to report it
options.B: Leave the patient alone in a quiet room to reflect
options.C: Maintain constant supervision and provide a safe environment
options.D: Tell the patient to distract themselves with a hobby

explanation: You nailed it! Safety is always priority number one. Keeping a close eye on the patient and removing any hazards keeps them safe during a crisis.

question: Why is nursing ethics so important when caring for patients at the end of life?

options.A: It ensures that hospitals never face lawsuits from grieving families
options.B: It gives nurses the legal authority to stop doctor's orders
options.C: It removes all emotional stress from the nursing profession
options.D: It helps nurses navigate complex moral choices and protect patient dignity

explanation: Ethical rules are like your compass. They help you balance high-tech hospital treatments with true human compassion, making sure vulnerable patients are treated right.

question: If a doctor suspects a hole in the patient's gut, what type of contrast dye is used instead of barium?

options.A: Thick barium paste
options.B: Water-soluble contrast
options.C: Oily contrast dye
options.D: Air contrast only

explanation: Brilliant! Water-soluble dyes are much safer because if they leak out, the body can easily absorb them without causing a major crisis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why shouldn't patients cover skin creams with airtight plastic wraps unless a doctor tells them to?

options.A: It prevents the cream from ever touching the skin surface
options.B: It can trap excessive moisture and increase drug absorption dangerously
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling any local pain relief
options.D: It causes the skin to become permanently discolored

explanation: Airtight wraps act like an oven, trapping heat and moisture, which forces too much medicine into the body all at once. Spot on!

question: What is the main action of mifepristone in the body?

options.A: It prevents infection by suppressing the immune system
options.B: It stimulates strong, rhythmic uterine contractions
options.C: It directly softens the cervix by increasing estrogen
options.D: It acts as a progesterone receptor antagonist

explanation: You've got this! Mifepristone blocks progesterone, the key hormone that keeps the uterine lining thick and secure during pregnancy.

question: What usually happens when a healthcare facility does not have a clear organisational structure?

options.A: Better coordination among different hospital departments
options.B: Instant improvement in employee satisfaction scores
options.C: Confusion over job roles and delayed decisions
options.D: A sharp increase in the recruitment of new nurses

explanation: Without clear reporting lines, staff get confused about whose job is whose, and simple decisions take forever. A clear structure prevents this headache!

question: On day four after delivery, a breastfeeding mother tells you she feels overwhelmed and cries easily when the baby fusses, but she loves holding her baby and sleeps well when the baby sleeps. What is your best response?

options.A: Inform her that she shows classic signs of postpartum psychosis
options.B: Tell her to stop breastfeeding immediately to stabilize her hormones
options.C: Reassure her that these feelings are common postpartum blues and will likely pass soon
options.D: Immediately arrange an emergency psychiatric admission for depression

explanation: Tearfulness and mood swings in the first two weeks are totally normal 'baby blues.' A listening ear and gentle reassurance work wonders here!

question: How do money worries directly affect a patient who has been given a referral?

options.A: Patients may refuse or delay going because they cannot afford hospital fees
options.B: Hospitals automatically waive all bills for referred community patients
options.C: The government refunds transport money upon arrival at the gate
options.D: Patients receive double the amount of free drugs to compensate

explanation: So true. Because many people pay out-of-pocket, financial hardship often forces vulnerable patients to stay home instead of getting the specialist care they need.

question: Which of these signs often happens to a person right before they vomit?

options.A: Temporary loss of sight
options.B: Sweating and pale skin (diaphoresis and pallor)
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle shaking
options.D: Sudden high fever and chills

explanation: When the vomiting center in the brain wakes up, it triggers the autonomic nervous system, often making the patient sweat, look pale, and feel warm or cold just before emesis.

question: A patient in anaphylactic shock gets an epinephrine shot, but after 10 minutes they are still wheezing and have low blood pressure. What is your next nursing action?

options.A: Discontinue oxygen therapy to calm the patient down
options.B: Wait another hour to see if the first dose takes effect
options.C: Give oral antihistamines instead of further injections
options.D: Administer a second dose of intramuscular epinephrine

explanation: Well done! If symptoms don't clear up, it is completely safe and necessary to give a repeat dose of epinephrine every 5 to 15 minutes while waiting for advanced help.

question: When does a polyvalent nurse need critical thinking the most?

options.A: When ordering food supplies for the hospital canteen
options.B: When organizing the staff holiday duty roster
options.C: When filing daily paperwork at the nurses' station
options.D: When analyzing sudden changes in a patient's condition

explanation: Exactly! Critical thinking helps you spot trouble early, figure out what's happening when a patient suddenly takes a turn for the worse, and act fast.

question: How does educating a patient help reduce inappropriate drug use?

options.A: It prevents them from ever visiting a hospital clinic again
options.B: It helps them understand why they do not need certain medicines
options.C: It forces pharmaceutical companies to lower medication prices
options.D: It gives them the legal right to prescribe drugs to neighbors

explanation: When patients understand the risks of unnecessary drugs, they are less likely to demand them from clinicians. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why do many women hide complications from an unsafe abortion in communities where it is heavily looked down upon?

options.A: Instructions given routinely by hospital doctors
options.B: Desire to test their own physical endurance
options.C: Fear of public judgment, disgrace, and legal trouble
options.D: Lack of pain receptors in the reproductive organs

explanation: Spot on. Stigma creates a scary wall of silence, making patients hide emergencies out of fear of being shamed or punished.

question: Which childhood lymphoma is very common in malaria-endemic regions like Nigeria?

options.A: Multiple myeloma
options.B: Chronic myeloid leukemia
options.C: Burkitt lymphoma
options.D: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia

explanation: Burkitt lymphoma is well-known in tropical Africa. It's often linked with the Epstein-Barr virus and chronic exposure to malaria.

question: Which symptom is a very common clue that points specifically to COVID-19 over other flu-like viruses?

options.A: Sudden loss of taste or smell
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.D: Severe swelling of the salivary glands

explanation: Spot on! Losing your sense of taste or smell (anosmia and ageusia) is a classic hallmark sign of a SARS-CoV-2 infection. Easy to remember for your clinicals!

question: Which of these is a bad practice that can cause tissue damage when giving injections?

options.A: Rotating sites when patients need repeated doses
options.B: Using the correct needle length for the patient's size
options.C: Giving multiple injections into the exact same spot
options.D: Allowing the skin disinfectant to dry before piercing

explanation: Spot on! Poking the exact same spot over and over causes hard, damaged tissue and scars. Always rotate your injection sites to give the skin and muscle a break!

question: Which organism usually causes eye infection symptoms to show up the earliest, often within 2 to 5 days after birth?

options.A: Herpes simplex virus
options.B: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: You're doing great! Gonococcal eye infections act fast, showing severe signs within just a few days of life. Quick action saves sight!

question: Why is the pelvic floor shaped like a hammock?

options.A: To store excess fat reserves in the lower pelvis
options.B: To completely block all pelvic openings at rest
options.C: To anchor the major bones of the lower limbs
options.D: To support abdominal organs against downward pressure

explanation: Spot on! Just like a hammock catches you when you sit, your pelvic floor muscles hold up organs like the bladder and uterus against gravity.

question: What is a crucial instruction for a patient who just had cryotherapy (freezing) for symptomatic cervical ectropion?

options.A: Increase strenuous physical exercise to speed up pelvic blood flow
options.B: Expect complete absence of vaginal discharge for at least two months
options.C: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampon use for a specified healing period
options.D: Perform vigorous vaginal douching twice daily to clear debris

explanation: Pelvic rest is vital after cryotherapy to give the treated cervical tissue time to heal safely without introducing infection. Excellent clinical advice to remember!

question: Why do older adults often need reading glasses for small print?

options.A: The retina gradually detaches from the back wall
options.B: Eye fluid production drops significantly with age
options.C: The natural lens loses its flexibility over time
options.D: The cornea becomes too cloudy to let light pass

explanation: As we age, the lens inside our eye naturally stiffens up and can't change shape as easily to focus on things close up. That's totally normal!

question: What is the main reason nurses use cognitive screening tools during a check-up?

options.A: To identify the exact genetic marker causing the disease
options.B: To measure the electrical activity in the heart and brain
options.C: To measure specific mental functions like memory and attention
options.D: To provide a permanent cure for progressive memory loss

explanation: You nailed it! Screening tools give a clear way to check memory and attention, helping us see how much the brain is affected. Well done!

question: How do oxygen and glucose generally move from the capillary blood into the body tissues?

options.A: Rapid evaporation through tiny pores
options.B: Active pumping by white blood cells
options.C: Magnetic attraction to tissue proteins
options.D: Diffusion down a concentration gradient

explanation: Substances move naturally from an area of higher concentration in the blood to an area of lower concentration in the tissues via diffusion. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which lifestyle change makes the biggest difference in preventing oral cancer?

options.A: Avoiding all dairy products in the diet
options.B: Taking daily multivitamin supplements
options.C: Using hard-bristled toothbrushes twice daily
options.D: Stopping tobacco use and limiting alcohol

explanation: Smoking, tobacco use, and heavy drinking are the main culprits behind most oral cancers.

question: As a nurse, what is a key assessment to keep in mind for a patient taking an anticholinergic medication?

options.A: Measuring fasting blood glucose levels
options.B: Testing visual acuity every morning
options.C: Monitoring urinary output for retention
options.D: Checking deep tendon reflexes hourly

explanation: Spot on! Because these drugs relax the bladder and can make passing urine difficult, keeping an eye on their output is a must.

question: A patient with severe malnutrition is admitted to your ward. Why are they at high risk for opportunistic infections?

options.A: Poor nutrition compromises their immune defenses and breaks down physical barriers
options.B: Lack of nutrients stops medications from working inside the bloodstream
options.C: Their body temperature permanently rises to a level that fosters bacterial growth
options.D: Malnourished tissues attract higher concentrations of ambient airborne viruses

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Without proper food and nutrients, the body cannot build strong immune cells or maintain tough physical barriers like skin and mucous membranes.

question: A newly widowed patient comes to the clinic looking very weak, dehydrated, and depressed after weeks of isolation. What should be the nurse's first step?

options.A: Advise her to return home and obey the cultural rules quietly
options.B: Report her in-laws immediately to the local village chief for trial
options.C: Stabilize her physical health by addressing dehydration and infections
options.D: Ask her to pay for her hospital registration card before treatment

explanation: Spot on! Emergency nursing always puts life-threatening physical issues—like severe dehydration or infection—first before anything else.

question: Which sign is a strong indicator of a catheter-associated urinary tract infection?

options.A: Cloudy and foul-smelling urine
options.B: Extreme dryness of the mouth
options.C: Bright red blood in the stool
options.D: Sudden swelling of the lower legs

explanation: You nailed it! When urine turns cloudy, smells bad, or the patient feels feverish and uncomfortable, it usually points to a brewing infection.

question: During a vaginal exam, you suddenly spot an umbilical cord prolapse. What is your very first emergency action?

options.A: Manually lift the presenting part off the cord to relieve pressure
options.B: Send the patient home to rest until the next scheduled clinic visit
options.C: Administer oral pain medication and document the finding later
options.D: Wait quietly for the next contraction to see if the cord recedes

explanation: Every second counts here! By using your hand to lift the baby's head off the cord, you keep oxygen flowing to the baby until delivery.

question: What usually happens during the orientation phase of meeting a patient?

options.A: Rapport is built and the purpose of the interview is explained
options.B: The nurse summarizes all findings and leaves the room
options.C: The patient is discharged with written medication instructions
options.D: Detailed physical assessments and vital signs are finalized

explanation: Correct! The orientation phase is all about friendly introductions, setting expectations, and building that initial trust.

question: Why would a doctor choose a nasal endoscope instead of a basic speculum exam?

options.A: To stop sudden nosebleeds in the front septum
options.B: To measure air pressure inside the cheek sinuses
options.C: To test the patient's sense of smell
options.D: To look deep inside the nasal passages and sinus openings

explanation: Nasal endoscopes use tiny cameras and lights to see past the front of the nose into deeper areas a regular speculum can't reach.

question: Why is ovarian cancer often tricky to catch in its early stages?

options.A: The ovaries are located deep in the pelvis and early tumors rarely cause symptoms
options.B: Symptoms always mimic a common urinary tract infection
options.C: Blood tests routinely miss the specific markers of early ovarian growth
options.D: Ovarian tissue does not develop abnormal cells until late adulthood

explanation: Because the pelvis gives the ovaries plenty of room to stretch, tumors can grow quite a bit before causing any noticeable pain or pressure.

question: Why is obtaining informed consent mandatory before conducting any clinical examination or procedure?

options.A: It legally protects the hospital from paying any utility bills
options.B: It respects the patient's legal right to bodily autonomy and choice
options.C: It speeds up the admission process in busy maternity wards
options.D: It removes all professional liability from the midwife completely

explanation: Informed consent honors a patient's autonomy, allowing them to understand and decide on their own healthcare interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h7)

question: A nurse changes a contaminated needle but reuses the plastic syringe barrel for another patient. What is the big danger here?

options.A: It causes an immediate allergic reaction in the patient
options.B: It transfers blood-borne pathogens trapped inside the barrel
options.C: It causes severe muscle necrosis at the injection site
options.D: It neutralizes the therapeutic effect of the injected drug

explanation: Remember, fluids and tiny amounts of blood pull back into the barrel during use. Changing just the needle isn't enough; the whole syringe must be single-use!

question: What should you do to the skin before putting on a newly diluted medicated lotion?

options.A: Apply a thick layer of oil to seal the pores
options.B: Clean and dry the skin gently
options.C: Scrub the area firmly with an antiseptic pad
options.D: Warm the skin with a heating pad for ten minutes

explanation: A gentle wash removes dirt without upsetting the skin barrier. Nice and easy!

question: If a community shows both a high Maternal Mortality Ratio and a high Total Fertility Rate, what is the most likely link?

options.A: Contraceptive methods are causing direct medical toxicity
options.B: Frequent pregnancies without adequate spacing strain maternal health
options.C: Women are choosing surgical sterilization too early in life
options.D: Hospital records are systematically miscalculated by local staff

explanation: When pregnancies happen back-to-back without enough resting time, a mother's body gets worn out, which sadly drives up complication and mortality rates.

question: Why shouldn't you treat an undiagnosed megaloblastic anemia with just folic acid?

options.A: It destroys all existing platelets in the bloodstream
options.B: It permanently stops iron absorption in the stomach
options.C: It can mask B12 deficiency while nerve damage worsens
options.D: It immediately causes complete liver failure

explanation: Folic acid can make the blood look better while secretly letting B12 nerve damage continue to progress silently. Always check the root cause!

question: A patient says they can't follow their diabetic meal plan because fresh veggies are too expensive in their area. What is your best first nursing move?

options.A: Ignore the comment and repeat the original dietary brochure word for word
options.B: Advise the patient to stop eating vegetables entirely and take vitamin pills
options.C: Explore affordable alternatives like frozen or canned vegetables and consult social work
options.D: Tell the patient that buying fresh vegetables is mandatory for survival

explanation: Be a problem solver! Listen to their financial hurdles and help them find budget-friendly swaps so they can still eat healthy without breaking the bank.

question: Why must nurses strongly advise patients NEVER to squeeze or pop a vulval cyst at home?

options.A: Squeezing can introduce germs and cause a bad infection
options.B: Manual pressure forces the fluid straight into the bloodstream
options.C: It will instantly trigger cancerous cell growth
options.D: Popping it at home permanently removes the gland

explanation: Trying to pop a cyst at home breaks the delicate skin, lets bacteria in, and can easily turn a painless little cyst into a very painful abscess.

question: Why is it so important to keep protein intake up while on a low-calorie diet?

options.A: To speed up quick water retention
options.B: To preserve lean muscle mass
options.C: To stop normal kidney filtration
options.D: To block all carbohydrate digestion

explanation: Well done! Eating enough protein gives your body the building blocks it needs so it burns fat instead of breaking down your hard-earned muscle.

question: A patient is having a rising panic attack at home. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink several cups of strong coffee
options.B: Scold the patient for worrying over unimportant matters
options.C: Leave the patient completely alone in a dark room until they calm down
options.D: Guide the patient through slow, deep breathing exercises

explanation: Brilliant! Slow, steady breaths help lower the heart rate and calm down hyperventilation. Nursing care at its finest!

question: Which food group is the best natural source of dietary fiber to promote healthy bowel movements?

options.A: Fatty red meats and processed dairy products
options.B: Processed white bread and refined white rice
options.C: Fresh fruits, vegetables, and whole grains
options.D: Clear sugary beverages and bottled juices

explanation: Plant-based foods and whole grains contain high amounts of natural fiber, which bulks stool and stimulates regular elimination. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is it helpful to feel (palpate) the patient's lower belly before doing a catheterisation?

options.A: To stimulate the urethral sphincter to open
options.B: To check if the kidneys are infected
options.C: To measure the exact length of the urethra
options.D: To confirm the presence of a full, distended bladder

explanation: Spot on! Feeling the lower belly (suprapubic area) lets you check if urine is actually backed up and trapped in the bladder, confirming you really need to catheterize.
